mentl/b4a28c0:
The sweep's last open question — an init performing the effect its own
handler handles — measured to a gate finding rather than a row one.

The shape compiles and traps. `handler hf with s = g()` handling g, installed
by `fn main(q) = (g()) ~> hf`: mentl check is silent, 38467 bytes of WAT are
emitted, and the program exits 134.

The row is right, which is what makes this a gate finding. `fn m() with !F =
(g()) ~> hf` refuses with `!F + Any vs F`, so the init's F genuinely escapes
its own handler — correct, since the tee adds row(h) after subtracting
handled(h), and an init runs before its install exists.

Four cases, one inconsistency, each read rather than reasoned:

    pure init + install      main : -> Int          gate passes   runs, exit 1
    init performs foreign E  main : -> Int with E   gate REFUSES  —
    init performs its own F  main : -> Int with F   gate passes   traps 134
    no install at all        main : -> Int with F   gate REFUSES  —

Rows two and three carry the same shape of fact and differ only in whether a
handler for that effect exists in scope. The row is sufficient in all four.

The condition is found and deliberate. report_unhandled_names clears a name
when it is not strict and IS installed somewhere, and its own comment states
the trade: dynamic installs cover it at runtime, and the row alone cannot
split a dead extent from live dynamic coverage, which band A owns.

So it is a new face of a rule the crown already pins. Install-extent
exactness says an op after the install closed is unabsorbed and that crucible
passes; an op before the extent opens is the mirror, and the state init is
the shape that reaches it — which is why the previous two landings, having
put the init's row on r_handle, are what made this visible at all.

contribution so the gate will not credit an install against it, the general

mentl/b4cf433:
bind_handler_config_params records the Reason LetBinding(name,
Declared(hname)) when it env-extends each config param, which promised a
one-site fix: lower reads the VarRef node's Reason, sees the handler,
emits LUpval(0, slot). No walker, no frame, one site, Carried-Truth
exactly.

The medium refused it. At the init's config use the address answers
"start : Int" with "Why: resume carries the continuation input"; at the
config declaration it answers "start) : _ — still free", "Why:
placeholder". The env scope holding that binding is gone by lower time
and the node's Reason is a different reason, so there is no live fact to
read. Killed before a byte changed, which is what the acting-gate is for.

What structurally prevents the build, in one sentence as the dry-
iteration rule owes: the config-slot resolution is not a graph fact, so
every remaining route needs either new walk machinery over the init — 39
LowExpr arms that the column arc plans to delete — or context threaded
into lower_expr's shared VarRef arm, the frame whose failure in the
demand walk is still unmeasured. Neither is a small correct change today.

The ultimate form is the column arc's own move: put the config-slot
resolution in a column, written where infer binds the param, read live
at lower. Then lower needs no scope, no frame and no walker, the nested
case works by construction, and lower_state_init's special case
dissolves instead of being extended. Four designs died in this arc
because they tried to reach a fact the graph never wrote down. Writing
it down is the fix.

follow-up from the release that shipped it.

- bot: a dropped fang walked at unconditionally, and that branch
  preempts both recall and throw. steer() refuses the edge cushion and
  cover's padded rings, so a fang settled in either was one the bot was
  permitted to want and forbidden to reach — want and refusal alternated

  fang is genuinely reachable (clear box, clear rings, clear straight
  corridor); otherwise the bot pulses THROW and hold-recalls it, which
  the sim already supports. Policy-only, no SIM_VERSION bump.

  mid-string, over the live table, while the actual tap zones are the
  full left/right screen halves. Group headers sat almost equidistant
  between the group above and their own rows. Rows are now bordered
  boxes in the shared button language, arrows as their own entities
  parked at the box ends, headers pulled onto their group.

  unscannable. Now 330 with a SCAN TO JOIN caption; checked clear of
  the portrait and screen edge at 1080x2400 and 1920x1080.

noodles/b4d86e4:
The reverb send already highpasses its input at 200 Hz to keep kicks and
808 subs out of the tail; the echo had no such filter, so dialing it in
piled low end into the feedback loop and muddied the repeats. Add a
matching highpass at 160 Hz — a touch lower, since echo repeats carry
more melodic body than a reverb wash. Only audible when a track's echo
send is turned up (sends default to off), so it's latent hygiene on an
existing feature, not a change to the cold-open sound.
